analysis.summary: Chris led the call by listing product features but did not surface Emma's onboarding specifics. Emma stated her primary pain was faster rep onboarding and asked how the product would help, but the rep responded with more feature statements rather than tying value to her problem. The call ended with Emma agreeing to receive more materials.
analysis.next_steps: Chris to send more materials after the call (tailored to onboarding use cases); schedule a follow-up/demo once Emma reviews materials.
strengths: Named several product capabilities (AI summaries, dashboards, integrations) so Emma knows feature scope.
Offered to follow up with materials after the call, creating an opportunity to re-engage.
Mentioned integrations (Slack, CRM) that may be relevant to an Operations Manager.
areas_for_improvement: Ask open-ended discovery questions to surface onboarding specifics (e.g., current onboarding time, steps, biggest failure points).
Stop feature-dumping — translate features into specific onboarding outcomes and ROI for an Operations Manager.
Use follow-up questions and examples to validate what "onboarding faster" means for Emma rather than assuming dashboards alone will solve it.
Confirm next-step commitments (date/time for follow-up or demo) and identify other stakeholders involved in onboarding decisions.
Gather metrics and success criteria (acceptable time-to-productivity, churn during ramp, number of reps) to tailor the proposal.
action_items: Send tailored materials focused specifically on reducing ramp time, including case studies and quantified results for onboarding improvements.
Request Emma's current onboarding KPIs (time to productivity, training steps, tools used) in the follow-up email.
Propose a short (30-minute) demo showing onboarding-specific flows and how dashboards/coaching insights shorten ramp time, and offer 2–3 time slots.
Ask Emma to identify other decision-makers (HR, sales manager, L&D) to include in the next meeting.
Prepare a one-page ROI example projecting reduced onboarding time and cost savings using Emma's provided metrics.

The rep failed to connect features to that specific pain or ask diagnostic questions, so the prospect remained unconvinced and only agreed to receive more materials. No concrete follow-up meeting or next-step to validate fit was scheduled during the call.
